paper_title: Can LLMs Solve longer Math Word Problems Better

model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between a discrete variable on the x-axis, ranging from 0 to 4, and “Informativeness” on the y-axis, which spans from approximately 0.918 to 0.952. The x-axis is linear, marked with integer ticks at 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4. The y-axis is also linear, with major gridlines and labels at 0.920, 0.930, 0.940, and 0.950. Two methods are compared: “0-CoT,” represented by a blue dashed line with circular markers, and “CoRe,” shown as an orange solid line with triangular markers. At x=0, both methods start near 0.951. From x=0 to x=1, both remain nearly flat, with 0-CoT slightly below CoRe. At x=2, 0-CoT drops to approximately 0.939, while CoRe is at about 0.938. At x=3, 0-CoT is around 0.927 and CoRe is slightly lower at ~0.926. By x=4, both converge near 0.918. The plot suggests that informativeness decreases as the x-value increases beyond 1, with both methods following a similar downward trend after that point.
